prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1213; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light and was struck from behind by the third-party vehicle. Police report requested. Insured reports no prior claims involving this vehicle's rear bumper. Photos of both vehicles uploaded to the file.

Entry 2: Third-party driver's carrier acknowledged liability coverage and assigned its own adjuster. Liability appears clear based on the police report and driver statements. Claimant's bodily injury claim has been referred to the injury unit. Claimant is represented by counsel, so all further contact must go through the attorney's office.

Entry 3: Received letter of representation from claimant's attorney. Requested medical authorizations and the claimant's treatment records to date. Attorney advises claimant has ongoing shoulder pain and has been referred for physical therapy. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect the anticipated medical course.

Entry 4: Attorney's office sent records from the initial emergency visit and a follow-up with an orthopedic provider. Records indicate a diagnosed shoulder strain with possible rotator cuff involvement, pending further imaging. Requested the MRI report and the physical therapy treatment notes. Claimant has not yet returned to full work duties according to counsel.

Entry 5: Spoke with claimant's attorney regarding the status of the file. Attorney indicated a demand package will follow once treatment is complete. Advised that the carrier will review the demand upon receipt and may request an independent medical review. Diary set for follow-up on pending imaging results and outstanding bills. File remains open with liability accepted and damages under evaluation.
